lines.japanese: あ、どーもどーも死神サン、しばらくぶりっすー。その後調子どう？　やってる？
lines.english: Ah, Mr. Grim Reaper! Good to see you—it’s been a while. So, how’ve you been? Keeping busy?

lines.japanese: んー、そうなんだー、へぇー。
lines.english: Mm. Really? Huh.

lines.japanese: こっちはね、ぼちぼちっすよ。なんとなくね、こう上手く回ってるカンジ？
lines.english: Me? Oh, I’m getting by. Somehow, you know, things seem to be running pretty smoothly.

lines.japanese: あー、それでやっぱり、もうそろそろ……なんすかね？　お迎え。や、もうちょっとまあ、猶予があるとありがたいっていうか……。
lines.english: Ah. So does that mean it’s almost... time? For you to come collect me? I’d appreciate a little more leeway, if possible...

lines.japanese: いえ、なんか未練があるってわけでもないんですけど、ね。最期くらいはもうちょっと楽しませてもらっても、ね。
lines.english: No, it’s not like I have any unfinished business. Still, I wouldn’t mind enjoying myself a little longer before the end.

lines.japanese: しぃーん……。
lines.english: Siiilence...

lines.japanese: ええ、もうそろそろこっちもね、分かってきましたよその反応。アレでしょ？　こういう、すっぽぽーん！　みたいなノリ嫌いなんすよね。
lines.english: Yes, I’m beginning to understand that reaction. You don’t care for this whole whoop-de-doo, strip-down-and-cut-loose routine, do you?

lines.japanese: イエイエ、いいんですよう。その方がこっちもやり甲斐あるってもんです。チクショてめ、ぜってー最期までに一度笑わせてやっかんな！
lines.english: No, no, that’s perfectly fine. Gives me something to work toward. Damn you—I’ll make you laugh at least once before I die!

lines.japanese: みたいな？
lines.english: Something like that?

lines.japanese: ああそうそう、ワタクシ出番にはまだもう少し時間ありますんで、良かったらお茶でもお淹れしましょうか？　あ、それともコーヒー？　紅茶？　ホットチョコ？
lines.english: Oh, right. I still have a little time before my entrance. If you like, shall I make you something? Green tea? Coffee? Black tea? Hot chocolate?

lines.japanese: はっはー！　なんつって、だから、ここにはないって言ってんだろそんなもん。
lines.english: Hah! Just kidding. I told you, we don’t have anything like that here.

lines.japanese: っと？
lines.english: Hm?

lines.japanese: これは……聖騎士の呼子、ですね。
lines.english: That is... the Holy Knight’s whistle.

lines.japanese: てことは、あらら、タカシ君がまた逃げちゃったんだ。
lines.english: Which means—oh dear. Takashi has run away again.

lines.japanese: えー、すいません、話の途中でしたけど、どうやら≪スクランブル≫みたいなんでちょいと失礼します。
lines.english: Sorry to leave in the middle of our conversation, but it looks like a *Scramble*. Excuse me for a moment.

lines.japanese: ま、話の続きはね、そこからでもゆっくり見てってくださいな。
lines.english: You can watch the rest of our little talk at your leisure from there.

lines.japanese: 出来れば一生そこにいてくれると有難いんすけどねえ死神サン！　はは！
lines.english: Though I’d be grateful if you stayed there for the rest of my life, Mr. Grim Reaper! Hah!

lines.japanese: 「羽田君？　大丈夫？　顔真っ白だよ！？」
lines.english: “Haneda? Are you all right? Your face is completely white!”

lines.japanese: 女性の声が聞こえました。
lines.english: I heard a woman’s voice.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、こっちの世界は息苦しい……」
lines.english: “Ah... It’s hard to breathe in this world...”

lines.japanese: それに答えるタカシ君の声も聞こえてきます。
lines.english: I could hear Takashi answering her too.

lines.japanese: それは耳介から蝸牛神経を経て脳の聴覚野へ伝えられた分子の震え。つまり俺たちが≪面談≫で交わすような声なき声ではなく、外部から入りこんできた「声」。
lines.english: They were vibrations of air molecules, traveling through the outer ear and cochlear nerve into the brain’s auditory cortex. In other words, not the soundless voices we exchanged during an Interview, but a voice entering from outside.

lines.japanese: ふむ。ここにいて外からの音を認識できるってことは、どうやらまだタカシ君が≪コックピット≫を降りきってないようです。
lines.english: Hmm. If I could still perceive sounds from outside while I was here, Takashi had apparently not climbed all the way out of the *Cockpit*.

lines.japanese: いつものように現実逃避の旅へ出ようとしたものの、直前に何かがあって思いとどまっている──ってカンジですかね。
lines.english: He had set out on his usual journey of escape from reality, only for something at the last moment to make him hesitate—or so it seemed.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと……ちょっとだけ、行ってくるね……」
lines.english: “I’m going... just for a little while...”

lines.japanese: 「行くって、どこに」
lines.english: “Going where?”

lines.japanese: 「グレタガルドだよ……早く行かなくちゃ……」
lines.english: “Gretagard... I have to hurry...”
What!?

lines.japanese: ちょ、ちょっとちょっとタカシ君っ？　いま君グレタガルドとか言ってるよ！？
lines.english: W-wait, wait, Takashi! You just said “Gretagard” out loud!

lines.japanese: いいの？　よくないよね？　いいわけないよね！　ダメでしょそんなことバラしちゃ！
lines.english: Is that all right? It isn’t, is it? Of course it isn’t! You can’t go revealing something like that!

lines.japanese: え、まさか？　もうすでにいろいろ喋っちゃった？
lines.english: Wait. Don’t tell me you’ve already said all sorts of things?

lines.japanese: アッ、分かった！　それだ、その火消しを俺にしてこいッてんだ、そのための≪スクランブル≫だ。
lines.english: Ah! I get it! That’s the fire I’m being sent in to put out. That’s why I was called up on a *Scramble*.

lines.japanese: 「だって……僕たちには……」
lines.english: “Because... we...”

lines.japanese: 「僕たちには翼がないんだ……」
lines.english: “We have no wings...”
Whoa!?

lines.japanese: あー、びっくりした。急に来るんだもん……って、そんな呑気な場合じゃないのかな。
lines.english: Whew, that startled me. The switch came out of nowhere... though maybe this wasn’t the time to stand around marveling at it.

lines.japanese: 緊急の交替で引きずり上げられた際、まず最優先で求められる行動は状況の確認です。俺は自然を装って素早く周囲をうかがいました。
lines.english: When an emergency switch dragged me to the surface, my first and highest priority was to establish the situation. Feigning nonchalance, I quickly took in my surroundings.

lines.japanese: 白い空。教室。生徒。女子。ひとり。美空学園の制服。
lines.english: A white sky. A classroom. One student—a girl. A Misora Academy uniform.

lines.japanese: ふむ。放課後にクラスメイトとおしゃべり中、ってカンジかな。
lines.english: Hmm. Apparently we had been talking with a classmate after school.

lines.japanese: 「はねだくん……？」
lines.english: “Haneda...?”

lines.japanese: さっきの声の主はこの子か。やけに綺麗なお顔。いわゆる美少女だわ。外面から窺える内面は適度に強そうで、適度に弱そうで、いかにもタカシ君の好みっぽいひとです。
lines.english: So this was the girl I’d heard. She was strikingly pretty—a genuine beauty. Judging from appearances, she seemed strong but not too strong, vulnerable but not too vulnerable: exactly Takashi’s type.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、はい」
lines.english: “Um. Yes?”

lines.japanese: 呼ばれたのでとりあえず返事。とりあえず無難に。
lines.english: She had called me, so I answered. Safely. Noncommittally.

lines.japanese: さて、問題はここからだ。グレタガルドなんて単語を口走っちゃったのを、どうフォローしたものか。
lines.english: Now came the problem. How was I supposed to explain his blurting out a word like Gretagard?

lines.japanese: よし、今日はパターンＣ。ちょっと風邪気味で、いま熱中しているゲームの夢というか幻覚的なものがうっかり見えてしまったことにしよう。
lines.english: All right. Pattern C today. We’d say he was coming down with a cold and had momentarily slipped into a dream—or a hallucination—from the game he was obsessed with.

lines.japanese: そして速やかに撤退。これだ。
lines.english: Then retreat with all speed. Perfect.

lines.japanese: 「なにかな？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 方針が定まったので、タカシ君になりきって会話再開。
lines.english: With my story straight, I slipped into character as Takashi and resumed the conversation.

lines.japanese: 「なにかなって……平気？　私が誰だか分かる？」
lines.english: “What do you mean, what is it...? Are you all right? Do you know who I am?”

lines.japanese: 俺の目の前で手を上下に振る。へべれけに酔っ払ったおっちゃん扱いですか。まあ丁度いいや。
lines.english: She waved a hand up and down in front of my face. Was she treating me like a hopelessly drunken old man? Well, that suited my purposes.

lines.japanese: 「うう～、熱っぽくて頭がボーッとする……なんか昨日やったゲームの記憶がよみがえる……あ、そうだ、早く家に帰って続きやろーっと」
lines.english: “Ugh... I feel feverish. My head’s all foggy... Memories from the game I played yesterday keep coming back... Oh, right. I’d better hurry home and pick up where I left off.”

lines.japanese: 「続き？」
lines.english: “Pick up where you left off?”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、いま超ハマってるゲームがあるんだ。俺は勇者だ！　さあ戦いに行かなければ！　なんつって」
lines.english: “Right. There’s this game I’m completely obsessed with. I am the hero! I must away to battle! Or something.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃっ！　急いで帰るからまた！」
lines.english: “Well, bye! I’m in a hurry to get home. See you later!”

lines.japanese: 釈然としない部分はありますが、まあいいでしょう。
lines.english: The story had its holes, but it would have to do.

lines.japanese: 明日タカシ君がなにか聞かれるかもしれませんが、ただの痛い子だと思って、基本的には相手も深く追求してこないはず。
lines.english: She might ask Takashi about it tomorrow, but if she simply wrote him off as an awkward little weirdo, she probably wouldn’t press him too hard.

lines.japanese: だいたい今までもそんなカンジ。いつだったかの森里君って子だけは、思いの外しつこく問いつめてきましたが、それ以外は「ハハ……」みたいな愛想笑いで遠ざかってゆきます。
lines.english: That was how it usually went. Only a boy named Morisato had ever questioned me with unexpected persistence. Everyone else retreated behind an awkward little “Haha...”

lines.japanese: とくにあの高内さんとかいう子は──
lines.english: Especially that girl named Takauchi—

lines.japanese: 「多重人格なのかな」
lines.english: “I wonder if you have multiple personalities.”

lines.japanese: は？
lines.english: What?

lines.japanese: ドアノブを掴んだまま固まる俺。
lines.english: I froze with one hand on the doorknob.

lines.japanese: 振りかえると、あのタカシ君好みの美少女が美少女らしからぬ笑みを浮かべていました。
lines.english: When I looked back, the beautiful girl who so perfectly matched Takashi’s tastes wore a smile entirely unbecoming a beautiful girl.

lines.japanese: まさか……知っている？
lines.english: Could she... know?

lines.japanese: いや、知ってはいないけど勘付いている？
lines.english: No. She could not know. But had she sensed something?

lines.japanese: 「あ、帰るんだ。ばいばい。じゃあその話はまた明日」
lines.english: “Oh, you’re leaving. Bye. We can continue this conversation tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: これは……鎌をかけられているだけのような気がする。
lines.english: It felt as though she were merely fishing for a reaction.

lines.japanese: だけどこれは俺にとってある種の脅迫だ。おまえが話さないならタカシに聞くぞ。
lines.english: Yet to me it amounted to a kind of threat: if you won’t talk, I’ll ask Takashi.

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　なんか言った？」
lines.english: “What? Did you say something?”

lines.japanese: とにかく無視することはできずに振りかえりました。
lines.english: Unable simply to ignore her, I turned back.

lines.japanese: 「うん？　帰らないの？」
lines.english: “Hm? Aren’t you going home?”

lines.japanese: 質問に質問で返すひとは苦手です。
lines.english: I was not fond of people who answered questions with questions.

lines.japanese: 「帰るよ」
lines.english: “I am.”

lines.japanese: 「そ？　ばいばい」
lines.english: “Are you? Bye.”

lines.japanese: 喰えない女……。
lines.english: She was a slippery one...

lines.japanese: 俺は背中を向けて教室を出ました。
lines.english: I turned my back and left the classroom.

lines.japanese: だけどやっぱり引っかかります。
lines.english: But I still couldn’t let it go.

lines.japanese: もし彼女が本当に明日、俺の危惧するような話題をタカシ君に持ちかけたら──
lines.english: If she truly raised the subject I feared with Takashi tomorrow—

lines.japanese: ──それはまずい。
lines.english: —that would be bad.

lines.japanese: まだ彼はそれを受けいれられる状態じゃない。
lines.english: He was not ready to accept it yet.

lines.japanese: 例によってオートセーフ機能が働いて、グレタガルドへ逃げてくれればまだいい。だけどそうならなかったら……。
lines.english: If the Auto-Safe function engaged as usual and let him escape to Gretagard, that would be one thing. But if it did not...

lines.japanese: 「おかえり。忘れもの？」
lines.english: “Welcome back. Forget something?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は一歩も動かずにそこで待っていました。
lines.english: She was waiting exactly where I’d left her.

lines.japanese: 「まあね」
lines.english: “Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 俺は前髪に息を吹きあげながら元の席へ向かい、ふたたび彼女の正面に腰を下ろしました。
lines.english: I blew my bangs out of my eyes as I walked back to my old seat and sat down across from her.

lines.japanese: 「最初にひとつ」
lines.english: “One thing before we begin.”

lines.japanese: 「ある程度のことは話しましょう。その代わり、今から話すことは他言無用に願いたい、貴女の知る羽田鷹志をも含めて」
lines.english: “I’ll explain some of it. In exchange, what I tell you must go no further—not even to the Takashi Haneda you know.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は冷静を装って表情をほとんど変えませんでしたが、しかしまた興奮を抑えるかのように大きく息を吸いこんでいたのも事実です。
lines.english: She affected calm and scarcely changed her expression. Yet she also drew one long breath, as if suppressing her excitement.

lines.japanese: 「つまり、俺たちのことを知ったあとでも、俺たちのことには干渉しないでもらいたい」
lines.english: “In other words, even after you learn about us, I need you to leave us alone.”

lines.japanese: 睨みあうふたりの間、白い空に落ちてきた太陽。
lines.english: We stared each other down as the sun sank through the white sky between us.

lines.japanese: やがて彼女は、長い長い髪を掻きあげながら言いました。
lines.english: At last, she swept back her long, long hair and spoke.

lines.japanese: 「いいでしょう。彼に話しちゃいけない理由ぐらいは、教えてもらいたいものですけど」
lines.english: “Very well. Though I would at least like to know why I must not tell him.”

lines.japanese: ひとつの体にいくつかの人間が同居していること、各人にそれぞれの役割があること、タカシ君に与えられたそれは“無敵の勇者”すなわち何事にも屈さないこと──
lines.english: Several people shared one body. Each had a separate role. Takashi’s was the “invincible hero”—the one who must never yield to anything—

lines.japanese: ──ゆえに悲しいとか寂しいとか悔しいとか、そんな当たり前の感情を持てないこと。持てないものだから許容量を超えてしまうと逃げだしてしまうこと。
lines.english: —which meant he could not allow himself ordinary feelings like sadness, loneliness, or frustration. With nowhere for those feelings to go, he fled whenever they exceeded his capacity.

lines.japanese: そんなようなことを、ぽつりぽつりと抽象的に説明していきました。もちろん彼女が勘付いてしまったことへの、必要最低限たる釈明に留めておきましたが。
lines.english: I explained all of this little by little, in deliberately abstract terms. Of course, I gave her only the bare minimum necessary to account for what she had already sensed.

lines.japanese: 「ふうん……」
lines.english: “I see...”

lines.japanese: 「それにしても……グレタガルド、聖騎士ホーク、異世界への旅……まあ随分と喋っちゃったもんすねえ、彼も」
lines.english: “Still... Gretagard, Holy Knight Hawk, journeys to another world... He certainly told you an impressive amount.”

lines.japanese: 「や、そんなの、話したって普通は信じないと思いますけどね。ただ私は、三年間ずっと羽田君を見てきましたから」
lines.english: “Most people wouldn’t believe any of that just because he said it. But I’ve been watching Haneda for three years.”

lines.japanese: 彼女──渡来明日香さんは、以前からタカシ君の挙動に疑念を抱いていたそうで、いわく「彼には何かある」として、つねづねその動向に注目しておられたそうです。
lines.english: She—Asuka Watarai—said she had long suspected something was going on with Takashi. Convinced there was more to him than met the eye, she had kept a close watch on him.

lines.japanese: 「ふふん？　それは乙女な眼差しで？」
lines.english: “Hmm? Through the eyes of a maiden in love?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん……それはないよね」
lines.english: “Hmm... No. Definitely not.”

lines.japanese: あらら。冷やかしたつもりだったのに、ガチな反応が返ってきちゃいました。
lines.english: Oh dear. I had only meant to tease her, but she gave me a painfully sincere answer.

lines.japanese: 「気になる存在なのは間違いないですけど、それはたぶん、なりたかった自分とか、懐かしい仲間を見るような感覚だと……思うよね」
lines.english: “He definitely means something to me. But I think it’s more like looking at the person I once wanted to be, or an old friend I haven’t seen in years... if that makes sense.”

lines.japanese: 思うよね、なんて聞かれても困るけど、とりあえず異性として見てきたわけではないと。
lines.english: I wasn’t sure what she expected me to say to that. At any rate, she hadn’t been watching him with romantic interest.

lines.japanese: あら……残念がるだろうなあ、タカシ君。
lines.english: Oh... Takashi would be disappointed.

lines.japanese: 「でも私は普通じゃないんです。私なら羽田君と助け合って、いい方向へ導いて行けると思うんですけど」
lines.english: “But I’m not ordinary. I believe Haneda and I could support each other, and I could help guide him in a better direction.”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、お気持ちだけで結構っす。言ったでしょー？　俺たちに干渉しないでって」
lines.english: “I appreciate the offer, but no thanks. I told you, didn’t I? Leave us alone.”

lines.japanese: ぶすーっと不服そうに顔をしかめる明日香さん。お姫様みたいな顔して仕草や表情はわりと男性的です。
lines.english: Asuka screwed up her face in open dissatisfaction. She had the face of a princess, but her expressions and gestures were rather boyish.

lines.japanese: つい俺の知る誰かさんを思いだしてしまいました。この学園の美人さんは、みんなこうなんでしょうか。
lines.english: I couldn’t help thinking of someone I knew. Were all the beautiful women at this academy like this?

lines.japanese: 「遠慮しなくていいのに。自慢じゃないけども私、自分から他人の助力を買って出ることなんてそうそうないですよ」
lines.english: “You don’t have to turn me down. Not to brag, but I very rarely volunteer to help other people.”

lines.japanese: うわあ、ほんと自慢じゃないや。面白い子だな。
lines.english: Good heavens. That truly was nothing to boast about. What an interesting girl.

lines.japanese: 興味本位で首突っこみたがってるわけじゃないのかしら。本当にタカシ君のことを思ってくれて……？
lines.english: Was she only sticking her nose in out of curiosity? Or did she really care about Takashi...?

lines.japanese: だとしたらありがたい話です。いつもうちの兄がお世話になっております。
lines.english: If so, I ought to thank her. Thank you for always looking after my brother.

lines.japanese: 「明日香さん、ペットとかって飼ったことあります？　小鳥とか」
lines.english: “Asuka, have you ever kept a pet? A little bird, perhaps?”

lines.japanese: 俺は彼女の申し出を辞退した理由に、説話的なたとえを付けくわえることにしました。
lines.english: I decided to explain my refusal with a little parable.

lines.japanese: 「そこに羽を怪我して飛べない小鳥がいたとしましょう」
lines.english: “Suppose there were a little bird with an injured wing, unable to fly.”

lines.japanese: 人差し指で眼下の電線をぴっとなぞります。
lines.english: I traced the power line below with my index finger.

lines.japanese: 「でもその子は、自分が飛べないことに気付いてないんです。細いロープの上を、奇跡的にまっすぐ歩いてるだけ。なのに、自分も他の鳥たちと同じ高度の上を飛んでいるものと勘違いしています」
lines.english: “But the bird doesn’t know it cannot fly. By some miracle, all it is doing is walking straight along a narrow rope. Yet it imagines itself soaring through the sky beside all the other birds.”

lines.japanese: 「そこが危ない綱の上、ふと下を見れば落っこちてしまいそうな高さにいるとしたら、何も知らないでいた方が幸せだと思いません？」
lines.english: “If that rope is dangerous—if one glance down from such a height might send the bird tumbling—wouldn’t it be happier never knowing?”

lines.japanese: 隣りを歩くお姫様は、しばらく考えこむように口をつぐんでいました。
lines.english: The princess walking beside me fell thoughtfully silent for a while.

lines.japanese: ややあって、通学バッグを肩の後ろへ担ぎながらぴしゃりと一言。
lines.english: After a while, she hitched her schoolbag up behind her shoulder and delivered a single sharp reply.

lines.japanese: 「でもいつまでもそのまま放っておくのは優しさじゃないと思う」
lines.english: “But leaving it that way forever isn’t kindness.”

lines.japanese: ふん。正論を言ってくれるなあ。
lines.english: Hmph. Trust her to make the irrefutable point.

lines.japanese: 「たしかにね。一生その小鳥のそばに寄りそって生きてけるって、そこまで言ってくれるひとが現れたなら、俺はそのひとにお任せしたいところだけど──」
lines.english: “True. If someone appeared and promised to stay beside that little bird for the rest of its life, I would gladly entrust the bird to them—”

lines.japanese: 「──そこまでの覚悟がないんだったら、やっぱり干渉してほしくはないなあ」
lines.english: “—but without that degree of resolve, I would still rather they did not interfere.”

lines.japanese: 明日香さんは歩道橋の真ん中でゆっくり足を止めました。
lines.english: Asuka slowly stopped halfway across the pedestrian bridge.

lines.japanese: あら。せっかく仮初めの学生気分を満喫してたのに、楽しかった下校時間もこれで終わりかしら。
lines.english: Oh dear. I had been enjoying my borrowed hour as a student. Did this mark the end of our pleasant walk home from school?

lines.japanese: 「もっと話しとけばよかった」
lines.english: “I should have talked to him more.”

lines.japanese: 「は？　あのー、帰らないんすか？」
lines.english: “What? Um... aren’t you going home?”

lines.japanese: 「もっと早くから踏みこんどけば良かったのかもね」
lines.english: “Maybe I should have gotten involved much sooner.”

lines.japanese: 「えーと……あのー……」
lines.english: “Um... Well...”

lines.japanese: 彼女も彼女でなにか思うところがあった御様子。話をお聞きしたい気もしますが、残念ながらこちらにも都合があります。
lines.english: She appeared to have thoughts of her own. Part of me wanted to hear them, but regrettably I had obligations elsewhere.

lines.japanese: 非常勤バイトとはいえ、ようやく職場の信頼を勝ち得たいま、無暗に遅刻や欠勤はしたくないのです。
lines.english: Part-timer though I was, I had only just begun to win my workplace’s trust. I did not want to arrive late or miss a shift without good cause.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ明日香さん、俺は予定があるもんでお先に失礼させてもらいます。ええと……また機会があれば」
lines.english: “Well, Asuka, I need to get going. Maybe we’ll talk again sometime.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。そうね。じゃ」
lines.english: “Yes. All right. Bye.”

lines.japanese: お姫様はひらひらと手を振りつつ見送ってくれました。
lines.english: The princess saw me off with a flutter of her hand.

lines.japanese: 最後まで笑顔を崩さないでいてくれたので、こちらも気持ちよくお別れできるってもんでした。
lines.english: She kept smiling to the very end, so at least we parted on pleasant terms.

lines.japanese: 俺は歩道橋の階段を駆け足で下りました。
lines.english: I jogged down the stairs from the pedestrian bridge.

lines.japanese: 歩道に降りたったとき、ふと振りかえってみると、欄干に寄りかかって夕焼け空を仰ぐ明日香さんの背中が印象的でした。
lines.english: When I reached the sidewalk, I happened to look back. The sight of Asuka leaning against the railing and gazing into the sunset stayed with me.

lines.japanese: 自嘲めいた笑みの浮かぶその横顔。物思いにふける美人は絵になります。
lines.english: A self-mocking smile touched her profile. A beautiful woman lost in thought made a striking picture.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ……タカシ君、あんなにステキな友達いたんじゃない……」
lines.english: “Well... Takashi had such a wonderful friend all along...”

lines.japanese: なんとなく温かな気持ちになって、俺はしばらく地上からその背中に見入っていました。
lines.english: Warmth rose inside me, and for a while I stood below and gazed up at her back.

lines.japanese: 「パンツ……見えそうで見えないなあ……」
lines.english: “Her panties... almost visible, but not quite...”

lines.japanese: 「おはよざーっす！　今日もお仕事しに参りました、千歳ぬるぬる鷲介です！」
lines.english: “Gooood morning! Shusuke ‘Slippery’ Chitose has arrived for another day of work!”

lines.japanese: 「おっ、きたな」
lines.english: “Ah, there you are.”

lines.japanese: 「おはようございます。もう時間ですから、早く支度を済ませてください」
lines.english: “Good morning. Your shift is already starting, so please finish getting ready quickly.”

lines.japanese: 「はい！　今日も玉泉トレーナーにご指導いただけて幸せです！　いやあ仕事が出来るって素晴らしい！」
lines.english: “Yes! What joy, to receive your guidance again today, Coach Tamaizumi! Ah, what a wonderful thing it is to be able to work!”

lines.japanese: 俺にもね、いるんだよ。もっと話しておきたいひと。
lines.english: You see, I had someone too—someone I wanted to talk to more while I still could.

lines.japanese: 「きゃっほう、着替えてきまーっす！」
lines.english: “Yahoo! I’m off to change!”

lines.japanese: 階段をテンポよく上がる俺に、日和子さんは怪訝な視線を向けていました。
lines.english: I bounded up the stairs at a lively clip while Hiyoko watched me with open suspicion.

lines.japanese: ま、そんなわけで、延長戦があるみたいですよ千歳鷲介君の物語。
lines.english: And so it appears the story of Shusuke Chitose has gone into extra innings.

lines.japanese: ね、あなたにももう少しお付き合いいただいて。まぁまぁ落ちつくところにでも腰掛けて。
lines.english: Stay with me a little longer, won’t you? Come, come. Find somewhere comfortable and take a seat.

lines.japanese: もしかしたらここから始まる物語、だったりして？　なんつって！
lines.english: Who knows? Perhaps this is where the story truly begins. Just kidding!
